$comment: Desired security posture of Supabase Auth for this project. This file is the SINGLE OWNER
of these values (global Rule 12) — nothing else in the repository may restate them.
Why a file and not a dashboard click: auth configuration is security-relevant state that
lives outside Git by default. DEF-027 was this same failure shape one layer down — the
repository described a database that did not exist. A setting nobody can diff is a setting
that silently drifts, and every gate stays green while it does.
npm run test:auth-config              assert the live project matches (read-only gate)
node scripts/auth-config.mjs --apply  write this baseline to the live project
'reason' is required on every entry. A security setting without a recorded reason cannot be

uri_allow_list.reason: Two defects in one value. (1) The production redirect was NOT allowed: the app requests window.location.origin + '/app/dashboard', and the allow list held only localhost, so every magic link on production silently landed on the site root instead of the dashboard. (2) 'http://localhost:4321' was template cruft for a port this project has never used, and a localhost entry in a production allow list is a documented Supabase hardening finding — it lets a crafted link deliver an auth token to a local listener. Scoped globs replace bare origins.

mailer_otp_exp.reason: Magic-link and recovery tokens were valid for a full hour. That is an hour in which a token sitting in a mailbox, a mail-scanner log, or a forwarded thread is a working credential. Fifteen minutes is long enough for mail delivery and short enough that a leaked link is usually already dead.

mailer_notifications_password_changed_en.reason: A silent password change is how account takeover stays undetected. The template already exists in the project; it was simply never switched on.

mailer_notifications_email_changed_enabl.reason: Changing the account email is a takeover step, not a preference change. The old address has to be told.

mailer_notifications_mfa_factor_enrolled.reason: An attacker enrolling their own TOTP factor makes the takeover survive a password reset. This is the notification that catches it.

mailer_notifications_mfa_factor_unenroll.reason: Removing the victim's factor is the same attack from the other direction.

mailer_notifications_identity_linked_ena.reason: Linking an attacker-controlled OAuth identity is a password-less back door into the account.

mailer_notifications_identity_unlinked_e.reason: Unlinking the legitimate identity locks the owner out of their own account.

security_update_password_require_current.reason: Without it, anyone holding a stolen access token can set a new password and convert temporary session theft into permanent account ownership. The app has no password-change screen today, so this costs nothing now and closes the hole before one is written.

rate_limit_verify.reason: The sign-in and sign-up bucket: 30 requests per 5 minutes per IP by default, halved to 15. It is not a strong control on its own — a credential-stuffing run rotates IPs — but halving it costs a real technician nothing. See the CAPTCHA entry under known_gaps for the control that actually matters.

assert_only.$comment: Checked, never written. These are already correct; the gate exists to notice if that changes.

external_anonymous_users_enabled.reason: Anonymous sign-in hands an unauthenticated caller a real JWT, and every RLS policy in this schema is written against an authenticated tenant member.

mailer_autoconfirm.reason: Auto-confirm accepts an email address nobody proved they control.

mailer_allow_unverified_email_sign_ins.reason: The same hole from the sign-in side.

refresh_token_rotation_enabled.reason: A refresh token reused after rotation is evidence of theft; without rotation there is nothing to detect.

mailer_secure_email_change_enabled.reason: Requires confirmation at BOTH the old and the new address, so an attacker with a live session cannot quietly move the account to their own inbox.

security_manual_linking_enabled.reason: Manual identity linking lets a caller attach an identity to an account from the client. Off until a product need appears.

disable_signup.reason: Open sign-up is deliberate for a demo product. Recorded so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

password_min_length.reason: NIST SP 800-63B sets the floor at 8 and puts the weight on length rather than composition.

password_required_characters.reason: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. NIST SP 800-63B advises AGAINST composition rules — they push users toward predictable substitutions and are a documented net loss. Length plus a breached-password check is the guidance. This blank is a decision, and the gate asserts it so that a later well-meaning hardening pass does not undo it.

known_gaps.$comment: Recorded, not hidden. An incomplete security record is worse than an honest one.
known_gaps.password_hibp_enabled: Breached-password checking (HaveIBeenPwned) is a Supabase Pro feature. The free-tier substitute in this codebase checks the same corpus client-side through the k-anonymity range API, which never transmits the password or its full hash. It is genuinely weaker: it runs where the user is, so it advises rather than enforces.
known_gaps.security_captcha_enabled: CAPTCHA is the control that actually stops credential stuffing, and it IS available on the free plan. It is off because it needs a Cloudflare Turnstile or hCaptcha site key that only the project owner can create, and it adds a third-party script that must be reflected in the CSP and in the cookie policy. Owner action, tracked — not a limitation of the plan.
known_gaps.sessions_timebox: Absolute session lifetime, and 'sessions_inactivity_timeout' beside it, are Pro-plan features. On the free plan a refresh token does not expire on its own, so a stolen one stays valid until it is used out of order (rotation catches that) or the user signs out. This is the most material free-tier auth weakness in the project.
known_gaps.smtp_host: Auth email uses Supabase's shared sender, which is explicitly not for production and is capped at 2 messages per hour for the entire project. Every notification enabled above draws on that budget. Custom SMTP is free to configure and needs an owner-held provider credential.
